protocol.purpose: External-source retrospective applicability check after specification freeze
protocol.selection: Two original published geothermal well cases with decision, formation and operating/diagnostic observations, not used in current source-to-rule assignments
protocol.coding: Use reported stage/material/mechanism; leave unknown conditions unknown; separate analyst uncertainty/data assumptions
protocol.comparators: Intact-wall stress/failure screen for rock/flow cases; inspection-only diagnostic assessment for barrier cases
targets: Additional observations needed to distinguish rival mechanisms
protocol.independence: Sources excluded from current rule development. Published outcomes are visible during coding; no blinded input coding, prospective prediction or quantitative forecast accuracy will be claimed.

cases.name: Gross Schonebeck GtGrSk4/05 stimulation
cases.title: Hydraulic stimulation of a deep sandstone reservoir to develop an Enhanced Geothermal System: Laboratory and field experiments
cases.locator: Repository PDF pp.4-9; Sections 3-4; Table 1 and production/flowmeter interpretation
cases.unit: Six laboratory flow experiments, one stimulated research well with three total field treatments; two sandstone gel-proppant treatments
cases.provenance: Stimulation, deviated geometry, fracture/proppant conductivity and laboratory fines/embedding mechanisms are source-supported. Sandstone lithology is known but competent/weak classification and decision-critical thermal loading are not assigned. Data, uncertainty and consequence levels are analyst assumptions.
cases.observations: Laboratory proppant crushing/embedding and conductivity changes informed treatment design; field production and flowmeter observations assessed the stimulated interval.
cases.comparator: Intact-wall stress/failure screening does not represent proppant-supported conductivity; this is a conceptual comparator, not a rerun calibrated field model.
cases.evaluation: Partial mechanism coverage: fracture-aware and particle assessment are selected, but no specific proppant-pack/contact, fracture-closure or chemical conductivity law is selected. The source does not establish that every mandatory layer improves the decision.
cases.implication: Use contact/closure and rock-proppant conductivity tests and interval flow observations to choose a stimulation model; no selector-induced field decision or treatment-effect estimate.
cases.limit: One programme and laboratory analogues; production improvement is not independent accuracy of the selector or proof of decades-long stability.

cases.name: Dezhou PYR1-PY2 reinjection
cases.title: Sustainable geothermal yield through effective reinjection: reservoir engineering case study of the Dezhou sandstone geothermal reservoir, North Shandong Plain, China
cases.locator: Publisher sections on large-diameter reinjection wells, water treatment, back-pumping, and Reinjection and tracer test evaluation (2012-2015)
cases.unit: Production/injection doublet PY2/PYR1; one pumping test, three reinjection tests and a tracer test; the initial 63-day interval includes about 23 active reinjection days
cases.provenance: Reinjection, semi-consolidated sandstone and clogging/particle-management requirements are source-supported. Thermal decision-criticality and geometry remain unknown. Data, uncertainty and consequence categories are analyst assumptions; field denotes diagnostic observations.
cases.observations: Screen/gravel-pack construction, filtration and injectivity maintenance accompany measured injection/pumping responses; scaling, corrosion and gas management are also discussed.
cases.comparator: Intact-wall failure screening omits particle and screen blockage; no competing forecast or controlled maintenance trial is reconstructed.
cases.evaluation: Partial coverage: weak-material/fines assessment matches the particle component, but the tool does not prescribe screen/gravel design, reactive scaling, oxygen control or gas management.
cases.implication: Constrain grain/solids, screen/filter properties, fluid chemistry and interval pressure/rate response before choosing a reinjection or maintenance model.
cases.limit: Short-term injectivity and thermal observations are distinct from modelled century-scale sustainability. The source lists eight rate values while calling them seven steps; no step-count quantitative claim is used.
